key_takeaway: No change: 49.2 AMBER for a sixth day, 0.8 pt under RED. The weekend moved money, not demand: Meta launched ~$35B of equity (plus a planned ~$60B ATM) to fund AI capex (Confirmed), and Elon Musk says debt markets have 'almost entirely shut off' for builders without non-AI revenue while SpaceX closed $40B of GPU debt (Confirmed, first-hand). GPU rents set new highs (B200 $9.70; Ornn, Reported). One SOX close below its 200-day (~10,690; Fri 10,779) is still the only single move to ~50.8 RED.
pattern: Classic early stage of a capex bust: financing cracks while demand still looks intact. In telecom 2000–01, shale 2014–15 and crypto mining 2022, credit spreads on the most-levered builders and the unit price of capacity turned first; supplier volumes turned last. Today the levered edge (neoclouds, IPO candidates, Oracle) is under stress, but unit economics (GPU rents) and the supply chain (TSMC, ODMs, Korea exports) have not rolled. First monetization crack showing (C2 amber).
decisive: Financing window shut for good — lab/neocloud IPO pulled or GPU-backed loan default (T-15)
Hyperscaler cancelling capacity for demand reasons rather than grid (D2b), or Big-4 capex outrunning OCF while 2027 guides decelerate (T-16)
